page: OVHcloud d2-8 is a Discovery family virtual server instance configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor based on the Haswell microarchitecture, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation model, meaning physical resources are shared with other tenants. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration provides a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that the shared CPU allocation and older Haswell architecture limit the performance profile of this instance. In single-core evaluations, the stress-ng CPU test recorded a score of 917.98, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance reached 3730.94 in stress-ng, which falls into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a PassMark memory score of 1125.99 in the bottom 10% and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 35.67 GB/sec.

Given the shared resource model and lower-tier benchmark results, the d2-8 instance is structured for entry-level, non-critical workloads. It provides a low-cost entry point for development environments, basic code compilation, and lightweight web serving, where static web throughput reaches 2.96 GB/sec. However, it is not suited for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput cryptography, or real-time data processing due to the performance bottlenecks observed in memory bandwidth and CPU execution speeds.
